name: Razzmatazz
lede: Razzmatazz is a vivid, deep pink-red, a showy word borrowed from everyday slang for flashy excitement rather than coined for any pigment or place.

sections.title: A flashy word, an undocumented color date
sections.body:
Our only source for this entry is Wikipedia, which gives no coinage date or dye history for the color name itself, only the hex value [1]. The English word "razzmatazz", meaning showy, exciting fuss, is far older than any color use of it, but our sources do not document when it was first applied to a color [1]. It belongs to the library's "everyday" field, the catalogue's term for commercial and slang-derived names rather than dyes or pigments [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[cerise]], 2.6 units away and almost the same color [2]. [[dark-hot-pink]] sits close behind, and [[ruber]] and [[ruber]] a touch further off, both duller [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive matches this color across even a small share of its canvas, as photographed [3]. A color this saturated is an unlikely survivor on an aged, varnished canvas, whatever pigment lies under the paint [3]. The absence describes this archive, not painting generally [3].

questions.q: What kind of word is "razzmatazz", apart from its use as a color name?
True or false: our sources date exactly when "razzmatazz" was first used as a color name.

openers: Razzmatazz borrows a slang word for showy fuss, but when it first named a color is undocumented.

issues: Single web-sourced library entry with no coinage date; origin left undocumented rather than guessed.
